title: Host the upstream worker with acknowledged startup and drain
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Runledger already owns claims, leases and durable retries. The process host must preserve that ownership while observing worker startup, failure and shutdown.

## Scope and ownership

Host the selected upstream runtime as one critical component of the reference root, consuming the command job type/payload and typed worker configuration. Use the exact startup witness from docs/reference-compatibility.md, not supervisor build completion as readiness. Lifecycle tests use the isolated fixtures and driven cleanup from batter-kjl. Signal upstream shutdown during process drain and await its owned shutdown/join result with the full documented budget, including abort cleanup. This task owns hosting; provider certainty/reconciliation belongs to batter-8q8.2. Do not supervise or respawn each upstream internal loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Startup/schema/registry/witness failure prevents readiness and follows partial-startup cleanup. A controlled initialization witness succeeds through the actual registered handler; acknowledgements state what that witness proves, without claiming every hidden loop initialized.
- Exercise normal drain and returned worker failure using the real upstream runtime and live fixture. Preserve the error returned by upstream; where upstream returns only its first failure and logs later failures, document that visibility limit rather than promise Batter collected hidden errors.
- Request stop-claiming at drain before forced cancellation. An already in-flight upstream claim may finish after the stop request; tests observe/classify it and do not promise a linearized upstream no-claim barrier absent a verified API.
- Outer grace includes the selected shutdown API's abort-cleanup allowance. Dropping its supervisor requests shutdown/detaches in the inspected candidate and is not proof of join. Timeout/panic/forced stop retains uncertain transitive termination and conservative dependency cleanup.
- Each job attempt gets fresh OperationContext budget and trusted dependencies independent of the submitting request token/deadline. Business denial and durable retry/reconcile outcomes remain successful task values rather than fatal process Err.
- Record upstream attempts and handler invocations independently; local replay does not multiply durable attempts. Provider-effect identity/restart proof remains batter-8q8.2.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (new unpublished application package)
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md
- crates/batter/src/lifecycle.rs
- docs/references.md

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Rebuild cargo build -p batter-axum --example http_service --locked and run python3 scripts/smoke_http.py --binary target/debug/examples/http_service in default, --signal SIGINT, --deadline, --warn-filter, and --warn-filter --deadline profiles. Finish backend work with scripts/jig check test and applicable Jig work gates. These commands do not substitute for this task's real database/provider/contract acceptance. Record exact versions, platform, prerequisites, commands and outcomes in docs/validation.md; missing integration prerequisites fail the explicit target rather than silently passing. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Re-audited against commit 22848ea on 2026-09-09. Process ownership is now extensively tested; durable job identity and reconciliation remain separate application/upstream contracts. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. Delivery authority remains this Bead; historical ExecPlans are not another backlog.

## Implementation handoff: 2026-09-09

Before batter-8q8.2, host an explicit probe-only registry containing the startup/control handler. Its witness may acknowledge the critical component, but the ordinary HTTP root withholds application readiness approval; delivery readiness remains unavailable. Test ordinary pending jobs prepared through the actual command path before this host starts. batter-8q8.2 enables normal application readiness only after registering and witnessing the actual delivery handler. Do not register a successful no-op delivery handler or claim ordinary delivery execution readiness; persisted delivery commands remain pending and unclaimed. Tests prove the witness completes while an ordinary command upstream job stays unclaimed and its domain state is not successful. batter-8q8.2 installs the actual delivery handler through the same host constructor. Recheck the selected Runledger registered-type claim filter; a catalog enabled flag alone is not the registry-omission contract.

title: Add per-attempt deadlines capped by remaining total budget
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A single slow attempt should be bounded without granting the next attempt a fresh total deadline.

## Scope

Add a source-compatible opt-in per-attempt maximum duration. Preserve existing `execute`/`execute_with_jitter` signatures, default behavior, and the meaning of their currently exhaustively matchable public error enums. Use a new opt-in entrypoint/result boundary for the additional typed attempt-timeout outcome instead of relabeling it as expiration of the original total context. Validate a positive representable attempt duration before any factory work. Immediately before each attempt, after its preceding backoff, derive `attempt_deadline = min(original_context.deadline(), attempt_start + attempt_maximum)` with checked arithmetic and downward cancellation. The input context may already be a shortened work phase; never recover its reserved finalization time or refresh the original total deadline. Reaching an attempt deadline is terminal for this execution, just like cancellation: it does not authorize another attempt or invoke expected-error classification. Preserve the latest earlier application error and the count of factories actually invoked. Keep panic propagation and destruction/cancellation behavior of OperationContext::run. Add a runnable example using distinct total and attempt limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Paused-time tests prove the deadline formula for the first and subsequent attempts, including a parent deadline shorter than the requested attempt limit, backoff consuming original total time, and use of a shortened `OperationPhases::work()` context. A later attempt may start with less than its requested maximum remaining; the maximum is a cap, not a minimum useful-work reservation.
- The opt-in result distinguishes an attempt cap expiring while total time remains from the original total deadline expiring. At a tied attempt/total deadline report total deadline; cancellation wins over either deadline, and an expired deadline wins over simultaneously ready work completion, preserving existing boundary precedence.
- Attempt timeout stops the sequence with no classifier call for the interrupted attempt and no next factory. Count only invoked factories: initial interruption reports zero, first-attempt timeout reports one with no prior error, and a later-attempt timeout retains the previous concrete error and actual started count.
- Cancellation during backoff or before the next factory retains the prior error/count without incrementing either attempt or future optional retry-token debit. A started attempt's child scope is cancelled and its owned future destroyed on completion/interruption; parent cancellation remains downward and no arbitrary spawned task is claimed joined.
- Zero/unrepresentable attempt configuration is rejected without starting a factory. No opt-in path catches panics as retryable errors. Existing public entrypoint behavior and exhaustive consumer matches keep compiling, and new public APIs have rustdoc plus an example.

- crates/batter/src/retry.rs
- crates/batter/src/operation.rs

title: Compose reusable isolated PostgreSQL leases with native pools
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Real PostgreSQL isolation and realistic fixtures are required to expose locks, database clocks and transaction boundaries that scripted values cannot model.

## Scope and ownership

Compose external harness leases with native SQLx pools in optional adapter-owned fixture support consumed by examples/reference-service tests, using the package/live runner delivered by batter-4t6. Consume native connection disposition from batter-7r3.2. This task delivers lease/pool ownership, ordered migration-bundle inputs, template fingerprint invalidation, connection budgeting and controlled database lock barriers using a minimal probe schema. Application row builders and application migration wiring are delivered by batter-8q8.1/batter-8q8.2 after the command exists. Do not require or invent a production router here. Generic batter-test-support remains a leaf; provisioning remains upstream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The adapter-owned lease/native-pool contract is exercised by the minimal probe consumer and removes duplicated fixture mechanics there. External downstream adoption remains batter-7r3.6; this producer does not depend on its consumer closing.
- Concurrent leases isolate probe state; the template fingerprint changes with ordered migration content/setup revision. Empty-database initialization and initialized-schema upgrade probes remain distinct.
- Minimal probe setup asserts affected rows and independently reads back intended state; downstream reference builders must follow the same rule and use the command migration entrypoint.
- Pool maxima plus standalone/administrative connections fit the selected harness connection_limits budget. One-slot pools and acknowledged lock barriers support complete-operation tests without sleep-based lock assumptions.
- Use the explicit ignored reference_live cases and runner from batter-4t6. Missing PostgreSQL 18/external harness prerequisites fail that invocation; ordinary all-feature workspace gates compile but do not execute live cases.
- Normal fixture finish explicitly closes every application pool before consuming the lease for cleanup. Deferred queues are separately drained; external harness shutdown() cannot stand in for drain_deferred_cleanup().
- Tokio paused time controls Tokio timers only. PostgreSQL clocks, transaction ordering and lock ownership use real database observations. Failure/cancelled-waiter ownership is extended by batter-kjl.
- Reusable ownership is public under the optional batter-sqlx test-support feature and consumed by reference tests; the default adapter graph excludes the external harness. Core and generic support remain independent; no Runledger dependency enters fixture support.
- Retained template reuse avoids repeated initialization; changed SQL, bundle order and setup revision change identities. A live changed-input clone proves changed state by independent readback, not only hash inequality. Ordered inputs and initializer ownership follow the readiness handoff below.
- Reject over-budget or overflowing declared connection plans before resource acquisition. Document separately bounded suite observers and harness-owned sessions; use a separately budgeted observer to prove the actual one-slot operation waits on the intended blocker and completes after explicit release.
- Finish closes every owned pool before lease cleanup; independent catalog observation proves database absence. Deferred drain runs after cleanup producers finish. Any retired backend used by the fixture tests is observed terminated before database release; no cancellation-safe teardown claim precedes batter-kjl.
- The exact live runner inventory includes every added fixture case and preserves all four compatibility cases, with runner controls rejecting omissions/skips/zero execution. Record both-toolchain live evidence and preserve the independent SQLx disposition suite.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

Consume native connection/pool disposition from batter-7r3.2 and the external harness public API verified by batter-4t6. Share demonstrated lease-plus-native-pool ownership and lock/barrier fixture mechanics in optional adapter-owned support, outside the generic batter-test-support leaf. Keep external provisioning, template cache/fingerprints and lease lifecycle owned by postgres-test-harness; do not copy Docker/database provisioning into Batter. Keep reference-specific rows, grants, migration contents and domain operations local. The basic SQLx helper can use an explicitly configured external database before this complete reference fixture exists, so there is no reverse prerequisite.

- docs/testing.md

Audited against Batter `662f2ba7271ba332f6ffdab0114d45ab59688569`, a clean checkout, and the Cargo-selected postgres-test-harness source at `3d525e6fc5745ce2e2437c7997de5cccdecff4ac`. The reference package already exists: extend it, do not scaffold another application. `docs/reference-compatibility.md` and the latest reconciliation section of `docs/validation.md` record the existing four reference and ten SQLx live cases on both toolchains. This audit inspected sources and recorded evidence; it did not rerun live PostgreSQL or establish that a historical disposable endpoint is still running.

### Concrete ownership and API boundary

Implement reusable fixture composition in `batter-sqlx` behind an opt-in `test-support` feature and public `test_support` module. Select the already pinned external harness with `default-features = false` as an optional dependency of that feature; the reference package enables it only as a development dependency. The default SQLx adapter graph must not acquire the harness, and core/generic test support must stay independent. Reuse generic `finish` where needed; do not move SQLx or harness ownership into `batter-test-support`. Update package guides and documentation that currently say the harness is selected only directly by reference tests. No Runledger dependency belongs in the fixture module.

Expose a fixture owner retaining the native pools and external database lease, with explicitly awaited normal finish. Keep SQLx `PgLease` (one checked-out connection) distinct from upstream `DatabaseLease` (one disposable database). Accept explicit harness/pool policy and application-owned initialization inputs; no ambient environment parsing in the reusable API. Keep minimal probe SQL and application migration execution in the reference consumer. A reusable helper must be exercised by that consumer, with duplicated lease/pool/finish mechanics removed where replaced.

Use an explicitly owned suite runtime/lifetime for the shared harness and retained template handles. Do not put SQLx pools in a process-static cache shared across independently destroyed Tokio test runtimes. Harness `template` single-flights on cloned handles, but its cache is weak: keep `DatabaseTemplate` handles alive for the reuse being claimed. The suite owner must outlive fixture finish and deferred drain. Choose the concrete suite arrangement in the ExecPlan without changing existing compatibility-probe contracts.

### Template inputs and executable oracles

Use upstream `FingerprintBuilder` and `TemplateSpec`, not another cache/hash engine. Define an ordered input contract with bundle identity, migration identity/type and exact SQL bytes (or the selected upstream checksum), plus an explicit revision for initialization behavior not represented by those inputs. Frame boundaries and order matter; never key by file path, migration version alone, or unordered iteration. The consumer's initializer applies the corresponding declared inputs through its native migration entrypoints, and closes initializer-owned pools on returned success or error before handing control back to the harness. A callback is trusted to match its declared fingerprint; this is not automatically verified by the harness.

Prove unchanged inputs reuse the retained template without rerunning initialization; changed SQL, bundle order and setup revision produce different identities. At least one live changed-input case must produce independently read-back changed clone state, so hash inequality alone cannot pass a broken template selection path. Concurrent leases from one template must have different database identities and independently isolated writes. Require affected-row counts and readback, not merely successful execution. Preserve the existing empty-database and initialized-schema upgrade compatibility cases; neither may be redirected through an already-current template.

### Connection and lock boundaries

Validate declared pool maxima plus standalone blocker/observer/admin connections against `connection_limits().connections_per_database()` before opening those resources, using checked arithmetic. Include observer capacity even when its connection targets the admin database. Document which connections are reserved per lease versus separately bounded suite resources. `max_simultaneous_leases()` is floor division; harness owner/template/lifecycle sessions are additional server usage. Multiple independently started harnesses do not share this local budget. Do not claim a server-wide bound from local permits or SQLx pool maxima; default retirement may leave server sessions alive.

Provide a controlled lock fixture with retained blocker/waiter identities. The blocker acknowledges actual lock acquisition; an independent, separately budgeted observer confirms the intended waiter is blocked by that blocker (for example using `pg_blocking_pids`), then release is explicit. The observer must not acquire from the one-slot pool occupied by the waiter. Prove the real operation stays pending while blocked and completes with independently checked results after release. Bound polling and the whole live invocation independently; elapsed sleeps or a helper-only lock check are not proof. Any interrupted/default-retired session used by these cases needs positive server-side termination observation before database release.

### Finish boundary and follow-up split

Normal finish joins/acknowledges test-owned direct operations, closes every fixture pool, then consumes the database lease for awaited cleanup. Only after all suite producers have finished submitting cleanup may the suite call `drain_deferred_cleanup`; the upstream barrier covers submissions accepted before it begins, not later submissions. External `shutdown()` remains a separate no-op and cannot replace this drain. Assert database absence using an independent observer after cleanup. Keep template caches under upstream ownership; do not delete databases by prefix.

This task delivers normal acquisition/finish and concrete resource ownership, not cancellation-shielded teardown. Do not export a cancel-safe claim or implement `timeout(fixture.finish())` and call dropped ownership retained. Keep errors concrete/redacted and preserve returned body/cleanup failures rather than introducing an early-return loss for the follow-up to fix. `batter-kjl` still owns the resumable cleanup driver, cancelled waiters, partial-acquisition/panic/owner-loss matrix, and systematic detached-session negative controls. Ordinary owner loss can trigger upstream destructive lease Drop; document that limit. Leave pools and lease owned together in a form that the later cleanup driver can retain.

### Delivery and verification

Extend `examples/reference-service/tests/reference_live.rs` with named ignored fixture cases, updating `scripts/reference_live.py`'s exact inventory and `scripts/test_reference_live.py` controls together. Preserve all four existing compatibility cases and the independent SQLx ten-case runner. Keep the independent process watchdog and fail explicit invocation on missing PostgreSQL 18/admin prerequisites, omitted cases, skipped cases or zero executed tests. Run new live cases on both supported toolchains against an explicitly selected disposable server; historical ports are not current prerequisites. Follow existing root verification and Jig requirements. Verify default-versus-test-support dependency graphs, rustdoc/examples, and updated integration/status/validation facts. No production reference router, application row builder, new provisioning engine, upstream modification, or reverse dependency on consumer completion is needed.

Readiness verdict: ready for implementation with these clarified contracts. No new blocking dependency is required; keep the delivery Bead open until implementation and its executable acceptance are complete.


## Acquisition ownership correction and review loop (2026-09-09)

User-authorized review follow-up extends this delivery with ownership of native lease/template producers before cancellable delivery, joins them before cleanup/drain, preserves producer errors even after waiter loss, and turns initializer panic into upstream awaited abort with its cause retained. title: Exercise cancellation and admission races under sustained scheduling
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Strengthen executable evidence for Batter's small native Rust/Tokio operational contracts: who owns work, what bounds it, who observes failures and when dependencies may close. This makes the foundation easier for AI coding agents to use and modify without guessing hidden framework behavior.

The existing tests cover specific failure paths and two 64-iteration multi-thread races. They do not implement seeded schedule exploration or sustained contention. In the 2026-09-08 audit of commit 5db16f6f18fd918d3d3558a68843120bf9a13b79, all 60 focused admission/lifecycle/operation/process-ownership tests passed a disposable variant that gave descendants independent semaphore capacity. A deterministic capacity-one ancestor/descendant probe passed on the original implementation and rejected that variant. This is a confirmed coverage gap, not a demonstrated production defect. Existing race-loop iteration bounds also do not contain a hung readiness/barrier/result wait.

## Scope

Add test-local seeded scenario generation, controlled scheduling checkpoints and sustained bounded multi-thread stress around completion, readiness, root/descendant admission, drain, forced cancellation and receipt/driver drop. Keep the current deterministic failure-contract tests and add regressions for discovered defects. Implementation fixes must remain scoped to demonstrated contract violations. Do not add a production scheduler, Effect runtime, DI abstraction, resource framework or new public API merely to support the harness.

The scenario families are admission/capacity, operation cancellation/completion, readiness/drain, task/report error retention, driver/receipt ownership and escalation/cleanup. Required cases must be selected explicitly rather than left to chance in a random sample. Keep harness implementation with the foundation tests; generic batter-test-support remains a leaf.

## Contract distinctions for the test oracle

- OperationContext children inherit cancellation downward. Finishing an operation cancels its operation scope; it does not join arbitrary spawned tasks.
- ProcessScope grants descendant admission while its ancestor is active. An already admitted descendant has process lifetime; ancestor completion invalidates further submissions through that scope, not the child's ownership. Roots and descendants share one queued-plus-executing capacity bound.
- Process admission is linearized with drain. Bulkhead cancellation preflight is not atomic with concurrent semaphore acquisition; admitted operations still need their own check/run boundary. Do not invent a stronger Bulkhead guarantee in these tests.
- Owned-driver waiter cancellation and last-owner drop differ from dropping caller-owned run_until. The former preserve the independently driven completion protocol on a live runtime; the latter requests emergency cancellation without promising awaited cleanup.
- Readiness observations and admission decisions must be judged using established happens-before order or contract-permitted overlap, not timestamps sampled after the fact. Likewise, eventual task success is not sufficient to label an abort request false.
- Retain only bounded, generic schedule metadata and numeric test IDs. Do not serialize internal reports or print Debug/Display of application errors/panic payloads. Test diagnostic redaction with synthetic returned-error sentinels and scoped capture; use generic panic-fixture payloads and account explicitly for default panic-hook output without installing library globals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a discoverable, bounded multi-thread stress profile for 2 and 4 Tokio workers. For each worker count, exercise at least 32 recorded seeds, 64 supervisor lifecycles, and 4,096 successfully completed finite tasks across those lifecycles. Require overlapping roots/descendants, saturation followed by capacity reuse, and coverage of every scenario family below; fail if a required family or workload minimum was not exercised. Counts are exploration minima, not correctness or throughput claims.
2. Prove shared capacity with a deterministic capacity-one case: while an ancestor occupies the only permit, descendant submission returns Full without invoking its factory. Under mixed contention, independently account for queued plus executing roots and descendants, demonstrate the configured bound, and check rejected factories remain inert. Receipt drop/cancel must neither release capacity early nor cancel admitted work; real completion must permit reuse.
3. Exercise root admission versus drain, active descendant admission during drain, descendant admission versus forced cancellation/task failure, and escaped-scope admission versus ancestor completion. Controlled orderings must check both allowed and forbidden cases; genuinely overlapping calls may take either contract-permitted ordering. A completed drain request forbids later roots; observed force/failure or an expired scope forbids later descendants.
4. Exercise operation completion, explicit cancellation, deadline and future drop with parent/child/sibling contexts. Check downward-only cancellation, parent deadline clamping, scope cancellation on completion/drop, and cancellation-before-deadline-before-completion when branches are simultaneously ready. Preserve the distinct process-descendant lifetime and Bulkhead preflight contracts stated below.
5. Exercise application readiness approval, every component startup acknowledgement, critical exit and drain in competing orders. Ready requires the driver plus approval plus all acknowledgements. Check ordered observations never return to Ready after Draining/Stopped, including acknowledgements/approval attempted after drain has completed.
6. Maintain a bounded test-owned ledger of submissions and expected outcomes, independent of ShutdownReport counters. Reconcile admitted successes, task errors, panics, aborts and unjoined work with receipts and the complete report; preserve all expected task and cleanup error identities/categories without formatting their contents. Mix concurrent failures and dropped receipts. Exercise shutdown-waiter cancellation during cleanup, last-owner drop with retained observers, and caller-owned driver drop before/after first poll under their different contracts.
7. Retain deterministic delayed-coordinator cases proving work finished before escalation keeps its actual outcome and is absent from abort_requested. Exercise completion at drain/cancel boundaries and real unfinished abort targets under stress. A later successful result alone does not prove an earlier abort decision was false. Panic, requested abort or unjoined direct work must keep dependent cleanup conservatively skipped; a joined wrapper proves nothing about detached descendants.
8. Bound each case's waits and each whole profile independently of application shutdown budgets. Configure a maximum 120-second profile allowance and an external watchdog deadline no greater than 150 seconds, plus explicit caps for tasks, event storage and captured output. A deliberately stuck fixture must fail visibly, terminate/reap within the watchdog protocol and retain bounded diagnostics even if Tokio cannot run timers. Watchdog termination is failure containment, never successful application cleanup; record observed timing and scheduler/OS limitations.
9. Provide commands for a fixed seed corpus, a single seed and controlled schedule replay. Record the seed, scenario version, worker count, case/iteration, action/checkpoint order and sanitized outcomes on failure, including watchdog failures. A seed reproduces scenario generation, not the Tokio scheduler. Demonstrate repeatable rejection of an injected fault from a recorded controlled schedule; preserve uncontrolled stress traces as diagnostics and reduce any discovered race defect to a deterministic regression before claiming it is reproducible or fixed.
10. Validate the tests themselves: the shared-capacity test must reject a disposable variant that gives descendants independent permits, and containment must reject the deliberately stuck fixture. Known-bad controls must fail for the intended assertion/watchdog reason, never just compilation or an unrelated timeout. Repeat the unmodified corpus in at least three fresh processes per worker count without retry-to-green behavior. Record exact commands, counts, toolchains, lock hash, platform, results and limitations; run required repository gates for implementation changes. Stress success must remain explicitly non-exhaustive.

title: Separate HTTP observation from request admission and deadlines
description:
## Problem and reproduced evidence

HTTP observation currently shares the request admission/deadline boundary. In crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs, request_scope_inner constructs the private HttpObservation before the readiness gate. Consequently, gate rejections are already observed, but probes and fallback mounted outside request_scope are not. A downstream consumer removed its outer TraceLayer during adoption and lost those HTTP completion events. The Batter HTTP example also merges probes after applying request_scope, so the coverage problem is reproducible from the recommended composition.

Investigation on 2026-09-08 executed against an actual downstream router using pinned Batter revision e5f2f04b2dbb349d08085caf177f662fcbc89812 and Axum 0.8.9. Its adapter implementation matches the local checkout apart from a platform documentation line. With an INFO tracing capture:

| Scenario | Response status | HTTP completion events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application success | 200 | 1 |
| Liveness probe | 200 | 0 |
| Readiness failure | 503 | 0 |
| Unmatched fallback | 404 | 0 |
| Method rejection on an application route | 405 | 1 |
| Drain rejection | 503 | 1 |

On Rust 1.98.1, all 16 Batter adapter tests and all six downstream HTTP tests passed. Their passing results do not establish coverage of this composition: tests/telemetry.rs exercises fallback by installing the combined request_scope across its router. Existing tests/scoped_dispatch.rs proves aborted combined middleware retains the original subscriber and nested span destruction, but does not exercise independent observation.

The disposable reproduction remains at /tmp/batter-http-investigation-zpp1c_u_/src/main.rs on the investigating machine. This is transient supporting evidence, not a required future test fixture; the matrix and assembly instructions here suffice to recreate it using generic routes.

## Delivery scope

Add independent HTTP observation middleware to batter-axum, with no lifecycle handle or deadline policy requirement. Keep HttpObservation private. Add an admission/deadline entry point that retains RequestPolicy, readiness admission, native OperationContext insertion, forced cancellation, and configured failure rendering. Preserve request_scope as a compatibility wrapper over the shared observation and admission implementations. RequestPolicy continues to combine readiness and deadlines; this task separates observation from that combined policy.

Update the HTTP example and adoption guidance to assemble guarded application routes using the admission-only entry point, merge unguarded probes and fallback, apply observation to the assembled router, and apply trusted server request identity outermost. The outer observer must surround middleware that rejects or transforms responses within the intended observed boundary. Migration must replace the inner combined request_scope when adding outer observation, so the supported composition emits one HTTP completion per request. Explicitly document the behavior of nesting the observer with the legacy combined wrapper; do not accidentally promise deduplication.

Preserve first-poll dispatcher capture using batter::telemetry::with_current_dispatch. Observation guards, instrumented futures and their nested spans must all remain inside its protected future through polling and full destruction. Preserve method normalization, matched route templates or <unmatched>, actual response status, outcome and latency, without logging raw paths, query values, headers, bodies, error contents or untrusted methods. Trusted request correlation remains application-owned.

## Axum composition constraint

Axum 0.8.9 Router::layer runs after routing and only covers routes/fallback assembled before the layer is applied. A route appended afterward bypasses it. A literal Tower wrapper outside routing sees no MatchedPath when the current observer creates its span, even for a matched route. Both behaviors were executed in the reproduction. Use the assembled-router placement to preserve sanitized route templates; test new routes added through that normal assembly path and state the late-route limitation. Do not describe the conceptual ordering diagram as literal pre-routing middleware unless route metadata capture is redesigned and tested.

Primary reference: https://docs.rs/crate/axum/0.8.9/source/src/docs/routing/layer.md ; also inspect the resolved axum source and record version-specific semantics in docs/references.md at implementation time.

## Ownership and limits

Owning package: batter-axum. Parent: batter-faj, observability across ownership boundaries. This work is independently actionable; it does not wait for database reference work, exporters, request metadata extraction, or the separate upstream admission integration in batter-97p. Related work is context, not a blocking dependency.

The observed lifetime ends at response construction. A dropped, polled response future may emit dropped without a response status; dropping a body after response construction is a different lifetime. Do not imply body streaming, WebSocket ownership, universal disconnect propagation, panic recovery, runtime-death finalization, or exactly-once log delivery. Library global subscribers and panic hooks remain forbidden.

## Required dependent updates and verification

Update public rustdoc and a compiling example, crates/batter-axum/README.md and relevant package guidance, docs/guarantees.md, docs/integrations.md, docs/status.md, docs/testing.md, docs/references.md and docs/validation.md. Keep API changes additive and retain existing failure-path assertions. Beads owns delivery scope; do not create a Markdown backlog.

For implementation, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Build the HTTP example and execute scripts/smoke_http.py in default, --signal SIGINT and --deadline modes. Finish backend verification with scripts/jig check test and applicable work gates. Record exact commands/platform/toolchain and limits; the investigation itself did not implement or validate the proposed API, streaming behavior or macOS behavior.

- A complete router composition asserts exactly one HTTP completion event for application success, application failure, short-circuit rejection, startup/drain rejection, liveness, healthy/unhealthy readiness, unmatched fallback and method rejection. Probe/fallback accessibility and response semantics remain intact during startup/drain.
- Timeout and forced cancellation preserve configured renderer status, headers and trusted correlation; observation records the actual response status without rewriting responses or adding execution policy to probes.
- Dropping a polled pending future produces one dropped HTTP event under the original subscriber with no fabricated status, no cross-registry panic and no leakage to the ambient subscriber. Test both independent observation without admission and the composed/legacy paths, including nested handler resource/span destruction. Never-polled futures do no application work and emit no completion.

title: Parse provider retry delays without shortening their lower bound
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Wire delay formats need explicit clock and overflow handling before entering the core monotonic retry budget.

## Scope

Add a small outbound-provider example with an example-owned Retry-After parser and concrete parse errors; HTTP parsing and date-parser dependencies remain outside the foundation's public/normal dependency API. Declare the new target explicitly in `crates/batter/Cargo.toml` because `autoexamples = false`; enable its tests with `test = true` and document `cargo test -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked` plus `cargo run -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked`. Verify the applicable primary Retry-After/HTTP-date protocol sections and selected date-parser version before implementing, and record them in docs/references.md. The parser accepts one header-field value: nonnegative ASCII decimal seconds or the HTTP-date forms required by that protocol. Use injected SystemTime for date conversion and return a nonnegative Duration; a past/current date or zero seconds is a valid zero floor. Malformed or unrepresentable input is a concrete parse failure; the example stops rather than silently turning an unreadable provider instruction into an immediate retry. Convert the valid floor once at the response/classification boundary; subsequent scheduling uses the unchanged monotonic OperationContext. Missing headers add no provider floor. Parsing never decides replay safety or failure eligibility.

title: Reject non-finite Unix process watchdog bounds
description:
## Observed behavior

`scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` accepts non-finite `timeout` and
`reap_allowance` values. Its validation checks only `<= 0`, so both positive
infinity and NaN reach deadline arithmetic in `_run_owned_process`,
`Capture.observe_until`, and `_settle`.

On 2026-09-09 on Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 with Python 3.14.7, this repository-root
control returned successful `ProcessOutcome` values instead of raising
`ValueError` for all four cases:

```python
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("inf"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("nan"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("inf"), output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("nan"), output_limit=1024)
```

The focused `test_scheduling_process.py` suite passed all 24 tests, confirming
that the current test inventory does not reject these values. The sibling
`parallel_process.run_parallel` already requires finite positive bounds and has
an infinity/NaN regression.

## Expected behavior

The bounded Unix process owner should reject every non-finite or non-positive
duration before launching a child. A malformed bound must not be able to turn a
watchdog or termination/reap allowance into an unbounded wait.

## Affected code and likely impact

- `scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` validates `timeout` and
  `reap_allowance` incompletely.
- `_run_owned_process` uses `started + timeout`; `Capture.observe_until` cannot
  reach its `remaining <= 0` exit with infinity or NaN.
- `_settle` similarly derives its cleanup deadline from `reap_allowance`.

This is lower-impact because callers are repository-owned test tools with
normally constant values. If a future CLI/configured caller supplies a
non-finite value, however, a hung child can hang local or CI verification
instead of producing bounded failure evidence.

## Verification limitation

The control used `/usr/bin/true` to prove invalid values are accepted without
deliberately launching a permanently hanging child. It therefore did not wait
through the unbounded failure mode. No Linux, hosted CI, or other Python version
was exercised for this finding.
acceptance_criteria: run_process rejects NaN, infinity, zero, and negative timeout/reap allowances before spawning; focused regressions cover both fields and preserve existing bounded success, timeout, interruption, overflow, and reap behavior.

## Outcome and rationale

Router unit tests and signal smoke tests do not cover actual socket, request-body and response-body lifetime behavior.

## Scope

Build real HTTP/1.1 transport tests around the current owned Axum server/lifecycle composition using loopback sockets. Cover an idle keep-alive connection, a request already executing during drain, an additional request on an existing keep-alive connection, a guarded handler consuming a deliberately incomplete request body, a response whose headers are sent while its body remains blocked, and client disconnect before and after response construction. Use controlled handler/body entry and drop acknowledgements and retained client/server task handles; elapsed sleeps are not proof that a handler or body reached the intended state. Exercise both cooperative completion and forced shutdown under active traffic. Use an outer process/watchdog deadline independent of the server runtime and configured grace, so a stuck server cannot hang workspace checks. Preserve the current response-construction boundary and write an ADR documenting the measured request/body/connection ownership and exclusions. This task proves and documents existing ownership; any production body-lifetime API extension requires separately scoped adapter work. Start with `crates/batter-axum/tests/http_lifetime.rs` plus test-owned fixtures; preserve the runnable HTTP example's purpose.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Record handler entry, response construction/header receipt, body completion/drop, socket closure, direct server-task result, and dependency-finalizer execution or skipping where applicable. Assert causal ordering rather than infer body or connection termination from a returned Response. For streaming responses, distinguish complete HTTP message framing, socket EOF/error, and body destruction; none alone proves the others.
- After readiness withdraws, a request which reaches guarded routing cannot start business work. An additional request on an established keep-alive connection during ordinary graceful server shutdown may receive the configured rejection or be rejected by transport closure; assert no business-handler admission in either case. A request whose readiness read already observed Ready may remain admitted, matching the documented linearization boundary.
- Add a companion admission control using test-owned synchronization: withdraw lifecycle readiness while temporarily withholding delivery of graceful shutdown to the server, then send another request on an established connection. Witness that request reaching the admission boundary and assert the configured rejection and zero business-handler entries. This prevents transport closure from satisfying every admission assertion. Keep the ordinary composition case with drain directly driving graceful shutdown; do not add a production API to delay drain.
- An admitted request survives drain until it completes or the existing force/deadline policy interrupts it. For incomplete uploads consumed inside the guarded handler, verify the response-construction budget applies. For pending response bodies after headers, prove that response completion/observation and cancellation of the escaped request context do not themselves own or finish body transmission.
- Exercise forced process cancellation separately from server-wrapper abortion. In the cancellation case, acknowledge pending handler entry, keep its request deadline from winning first, trigger process cancellation, and assert handler destruction, request-context cancellation, the actual infrastructure response/observation, connection termination, direct server completion and the corresponding cleanup decision. Do not assume that reaching the cancellation phase alone requires skipped cleanup if all owned work subsequently completes without an unsafe exit.

Retain and reconcile later body/connection teardown evidence separately. Do not infer detached connection termination from joining the aborted wrapper or let runtime destruction supply the observation.
- Test disconnect before response construction and while streaming, after acknowledging handler entry or response-header receipt respectively. Specify the client's socket action and distinguish full connection closure from write-half closure. Establish explicit regression expectations for the resolved transport, using resource drop acknowledgements and bounded observation checkpoints: distinguish a transport-driven drop before any test release, a resource still pending at the checkpoint, and a drop caused only by later teardown. title: Bound retry amplification with explicit retry-token policy
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A local retry-token budget can bound amplification but cannot decide external outcome certainty, user quota consumption or durable ownership.

## Scope and ownership

Add an optional caller-owned, finite process-local retry-token budget shared by clones; no automatic replenishment, wait queue, global budget, or durable scheduler. One token authorizes one extra factory invocation after the initial call. The initial factory remains governed by the existing total context and max_attempts and consumes no retry token. Select these consumption semantics: after ReplaySafety, expected-error classification, max_attempts, provider-floor/backoff, and cancellation/deadline preflight have permitted a replay, atomically consume one token immediately before invoking that replay's factory, with no await between successful debit and invocation. Do not reserve tokens during backoff. Cancellation or deadline expiry observed by the final preflight prevents debit and factory invocation. If that preflight permits the attempt, cancellation or expiry racing afterward may still allow atomic debit and immediate counted factory invocation; no await or second cancellation gate separates successful debit from invocation. Dropping execution before this boundary consumes no token. Once invoked, the token is permanently spent, including success, returned error, timeout, cancellation, or panic. ## Outcome and rationale

Joining a critical component wrapper cannot establish that its hidden descendants stopped. Completed finite-work and scheduling tests already cover the core ownership machinery.

## Scope and ownership

Reuse the existing subprocess/watchdog controls to exercise a component that owns internal tasks and a deliberately nonconforming wrapper whose hidden descendant survives wrapper completion. Verify actual initialization and transitive-stop acknowledgement requirements, returned errors and conservative cleanup. Do not rebuild the general scheduling or non-yielding harness completed by batter-953/batter-fvz.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Observe early Ok, Err, panic and forced abort with causal task/cleanup outcomes retained for the component boundary.
- Independently observe a hidden descendant surviving a wrapper that returns Ok during drain. The driver can report joined direct work and run cleanup because it cannot inspect that descendant; document why this is not transitive-stop evidence. Do not promise library detection or automatic cleanup suppression for hidden work.
- A conforming component acknowledges readiness after initialization and returns only after its owned descendants stop; contrast the observable outcomes with the nonconforming case.
- Use existing bounded subprocess isolation for actors that cannot terminate cooperatively. Preserve completed finite-descendant, abandonment and terminal-admission regressions without reopening their tasks.
